architecture.mechanism: Reducing aerodynamic drag force (proportional to Cd·A·v²) and parasitic powertrain losses by streamlining the body, minimizing frontal area, and decoupling accessory loads from the engine.
architecture.intervention: A lightweight, low-drag monocoque passenger car with a teardrop-inspired body, full underbody and wheel-arch fairings, active grille shutters, camera-based side mirrors, narrow low-rolling-resistance tires, and a small highly efficient hybrid powertrain with electric accessory drive and engine start-stop plus pulse-and-glide capable control.
architecture.expected_effect: Highway fuel consumption below 1.5 L/100 km gasoline-equivalent; drag coefficient below 0.15; total road-load energy per km reduced by 50–65% versus a typical production sedan.
architecture.falsification_test: Build a full-scale rolling body mockup on a production subframe and measure coast-down or wind-tunnel Cd·A; if Cd·A is not below 0.25 m² or high-speed stability/brake cooling fails, the architecture is not viable.
